# besttraveler

> besttraveler (https://besttraveler.ge) is a Georgian travel company that runs group tours from Georgia (Tbilisi, Kutaisi and Yerevan airports, or by minibus from Tbilisi) to 26 countries, and one-day tours around Georgia. Tour organiser: Natali Iashvili. Contact: phone/WhatsApp +995 579 57 56 36, email info@besttraveler.ge. The site is in Georgian (default), English (/en/) and Russian (/ru/).

Booking: a deposit holds a place; the rest is paid 15 days before the tour; money is not returned if the traveller cancels for their own reasons. Payment by bank transfer. Prices of flight tours depend on air fares and can change.


# Booking terms

## Booking and deposit

You hold a place on a tour with a deposit. The deposit amount is shown on each tour page. To confirm a place, contact us by phone or WhatsApp.

## Paying the rest

The rest of the price (minus the deposit) is paid 15 days before the tour starts. Some long-haul tours (for example China) have a different deadline — it is shown on the tour page.

Payment is by bank transfer to our Bank of Georgia or TBC Bank account. We send the account details when you book.

## Price

Flight tour prices are based on current air fares. Fares rise as the departure gets closer, so the price can change — book early and confirm the price before you pay.

## Refunds

- If you cannot travel for your own reasons, the money you paid is not returned.
- The money is not returned if you cannot cross the border because your passport has expired, is not valid long enough, or for another violation.
- On a one-day tour the money is not returned if you cancel in the last two days.

## Documents

- To cross the border you need an international passport valid for at least 6 months.
- For tours to Armenia you can travel with a passport or a Georgian ID card.
- Minors need a birth certificate, notarised consent from the parents and an international passport.
- Whether a visa is needed, and its fee, is shown on each tour page (under “Not included”).

## Airlines and weather

- The tour company is not responsible for problems caused by the airline (delays, cancellations, luggage).
- One-day tours run in any weather. A tour is postponed only if there is a problem with the road.


# FAQ

**How do I book a tour?** Call or message us on WhatsApp at +995 579 57 56 36. We confirm a free place and the price, then you hold the place with a deposit. The rest is paid 15 days before the tour.

**How do I pay?** By bank transfer to our Bank of Georgia or TBC Bank account. We send the account details when you book.

**Are flights included in the price?** On most flight tours the return flight is included. Each tour page lists exactly what is and is not included.

**Why can the price change?** Flight tour prices are based on current air fares. Fares go up as the trip gets closer, so it is best to book early.

**Which documents do I need?** To cross the border you need an international passport valid for at least 6 months. For tours to Armenia a Georgian ID card is also accepted. Children need a birth certificate, notarised consent from the parents and a passport.

**Where do the day tours start?** Day tours start in Tbilisi and go by minibus. The meeting point is usually the upper exit of Didube metro station.

**Do I get my money back if I cannot go?** If you cannot travel for your own reasons, the money you paid is not returned. See the booking terms for details.


# Tours

## India Group Tour: Rajasthan, Delhi, Jaisalmer and Udaipur

URL: https://besttraveler.ge/en/tours/india-rajasthan-delhi-udaipur/

- Type: By plane
- Countries: India
- Duration: 9 days / 8 nights
- Price: 4,800 GEL per person
- Departure: From Tbilisi airport
- Dates: 25 Oct 2026

A 9-day / 8-night group tour of India: Delhi and the cities of Rajasthan, including Mandawa, Bikaner, Jaisalmer, Jodhpur, Ranakpur, Udaipur and Pushkar. Departure from Tbilisi on 25 October at 23:45.

**Day 1: Tbilisi to Delhi and Mandawa:** Flight from Tbilisi on 25 October at 23:45, arrival in Delhi on 26 October at 07:05; Transfer to the hotel; after breakfast, drive to Mandawa; Mandawa havelis, houses once owned by wealthy merchants; Breakfast, dinner and overnight at the hotel
**Day 2: Mandawa to Bikaner:** Binsidhar Newatia Haveli, known for its bright, lively paintings; Gulab Rai Ladia Haveli, Goenka Double Haveli, Murmuria Haveli, Jhunjhunwala Haveli; Drive to Bikaner: Junagarh Fort, decorated with gold leaf, glass, mirror work and Dutch tiles; Breakfast, dinner and overnight at the hotel
**Day 3: Bikaner to Jaisalmer:** Jaisalmer Fort, standing about 100 metres high; Havelis with carved facades and windows; Salim Singh Haveli (17th century), known for its peacock carvings; Nathumal Haveli (1885) and Patwon Haveli (1805); Dinner and overnight at the hotel
**Day 4: Jaisalmer to Jodhpur:** Drive to Jodhpur, hotel check-in and free time; Mehrangarh Fort on a 125-metre hill, one of the most impressive buildings in Rajasthan; Jaswant Thada, a white marble memorial (1899) to Maharaja Jaswant Singh II; Evening: the Clock Tower and Sardar Bazaar, with textiles, antiques, silverware and handicrafts; Breakfast and overnight at the hotel
**Day 5: Jodhpur to Udaipur via Ranakpur:** Ranakpur temples (15th century), famous for their intricate architecture; Arrival in Udaipur, transfer to the hotel; Breakfast and overnight at the hotel
**Day 6: Udaipur, the City of Lakes:** City Palace, the former home of the Mewar rulers, now mostly a museum overlooking Lake Pichola; Jagdish Mandir; Sahelion ki Bari; Bharatiya Lok Kala Mandal; Evening boat ride on Lake Pichola; Breakfast and overnight at the hotel
**Day 7: Udaipur to Pushkar:** Brahma Temple and the ghats; Pushkar, a town on the shore of Pushkar Lake; Breakfast and overnight at the hotel
**Day 8: Pushkar to Delhi:** After breakfast, drive to Delhi; Free time
**Day 9: Delhi to Tbilisi:** Qutub Minar; India Gate; President's House and Parliament; Bangla Sahib; Agrasen ki Baoli, a historic stepwell 60 m long and 15 m wide; Dinner at Lazeez restaurant, then transfer to the international airport

Included:
- Return flights Tbilisi-Delhi-Tbilisi
- 30 kg baggage
- 4-5 star hotels
- Two meals a day (breakfast and dinner)
- Internal transfers
- Travel insurance
- Local guide
- Georgian-speaking tour escort from Tbilisi
- Group excursions
- Boat ride on Lake Pichola
- Entrance fees to architectural sites
- All taxes and fees

Not included:
- Visa fee (40 USD)

## Cappadocia, Amasya and Ordu: 6-Day Bus Tour from Tbilisi

URL: https://besttraveler.ge/en/tours/turkey-cappadocia-amasya-bus/

- Type: By bus
- Countries: Turkey
- Duration: 6 days
- Price: 1,350 GEL per person
- Departure: From Tbilisi at 06:00
- Dates: 2–7 Nov 2026

A 6-day tour of Turkey by comfortable bus. We never travel overnight: every night is spent in a hotel.

**Day 1:** 06:00 departure from Tbilisi (via Sarpi) to Amasya; Hotel check-in, free time, evening walk in the city
**Day 2:** Amasya city; Rock tombs of the Pontic kings; Amasya Castle; Avanos, an ancient town of craftsmen; Monks Valley, with formations of volcanic origin; Hotel check-in
**Day 3:** Hot-air balloon flight (optional), or photos with the balloons in the background; Goreme Open-Air Museum (10th-15th century churches); Silver shop (souvenir market), camel ride; Tokali Church, with a unique fresco that is the prototype of the icon 'Thou Art the Vine'; Uchisar Castle; Pigeon Valley; Turkish Night (optional, 30 EUR)
**Day 4:** Pasabag (Queens' Gardens): the cell of St Simeon Stylites and multi-headed fairy chimneys; the place where vines were first grown in Anatolia; Zelve, the Valley of the Monks; House of St George's mother (where, by tradition, St George lived); St Nino's village (Ortahisar Castle); Saruhan Caravanserai (1249); Pancarlik Church, one of the longest church interiors in the world
**Day 5:** Kayseri Castle, built in antiquity; Kayseri bazaar (optional); Gumusler Monastery; Ordu, hotel check-in; Ordu cable car (optional), with panoramic views of the city, the Black Sea and Boztepe hill
**Day 6:** Trabzon; Little Hagia Sophia; Shopping centre (optional); Return to Tbilisi

Included:
- Travel by comfortable bus (air conditioning, internet in Turkey)
- 4-5 star hotels in Cappadocia, Amasya and Ordu
- Breakfasts and dinners
- Qualified Georgian-speaking guide and tour organiser

Not included:
- Local fees (300 GEL)
- Ordu cable car (optional)

Optional extras:
- Hot-air balloon flight: 200-250 EUR (optional)
- Turkish Night: 30 EUR (optional)

## Hurghada, Luxor, Port Said and the Suez Canal — 7 Days

URL: https://besttraveler.ge/en/tours/egypt-hurghada-luxor-port-said-suez-canal/

- Type: By plane
- Countries: Egypt
- Duration: 7 days / 6 nights
- Price: 6,100 GEL per person (deposit 1,500 GEL)
- Departure: From Tbilisi airport
- Dates: 9–15 Nov 2026, 14–20 Dec 2026

A 7-day stay in Hurghada with excursions: Port Said, Port Fuad and the Suez Canal, a day on Hula Hula island, Luxor and the monasteries of St Anthony and St Paul. You stay in a 4 or 5-star hotel with meals.

**Day 1:** Flight from Tbilisi at 03:25; Arrival in Hurghada at 10:15; Transfer to the hotel; Free time
**Day 2:** Excursion "Port Said and the Suez Canal": early departure from Hurghada with a Russian-speaking guide; Al-Salam Mosque — one of the most beautiful mosques of Port Fuad, on the bank of the Suez Canal; St Bishoy Coptic Church — one of Egypt's best-known Coptic churches, where you learn about the history and traditions of Egyptian Christianity; Free ferry crossing of the Suez Canal, with a close look at large ocean ships; Salt Mountain in Port Fuad — a snow-white hill of sea salt, a popular photo spot; Lunch at a restaurant with a view of the Mediterranean Sea; Free time in the Port Said pedestrian zone for a walk and souvenirs; Port Said Lighthouse at the entrance to the Suez Canal; Site of the Ferdinand de Lesseps statue — the story of building the Suez Canal; Monument on Egypt Square, dedicated to the history of Port Said; Photo stop at the decorative gate — one of the symbols of modern Port Said; Return to Hurghada
**Day 3:** Free day; Optional safari (25 USD): jeeps, quad bikes, buggies, a Bedouin village, camels
**Day 4:** Hula Hula island: by yacht or by a large boat with glass windows (your choice); 3–3.5 hours on the island with swimming; Lunch on the island; 5-minute massage; Volleyball; Banana boat ride
**Day 5:** Luxor tour by tourist minibus with a guide; Karnak Temple; Colossi of Memnon; Crossing the Nile; Temple of Queen Hatshepsut; Valley of the Kings; Lunch; Return to Hurghada
**Day 6:** Monasteries of St Anthony and St Paul
**Day 7:** Free day; Transfer to the airport at 20:00; Flight to Tbilisi

Included:
- Flights Tbilisi–Istanbul–Hurghada–Istanbul–Tbilisi
- 20 kg baggage
- 4 or 5-star hotel with meals
- Transfers
- Travel insurance
- Local guide
- Georgian-speaking tour leader from Tbilisi
- Group excursions
- Entrance fees to historic sites

Not included:
- Visa fee (25 USD)
- Optional tours on free days

Optional extras:
- Safari on the free day (jeeps, quad bikes, buggies, Bedouin village, camels) — 25 USD (optional)

## France: Alsace and Paris — Group Tour from Kutaisi

URL: https://besttraveler.ge/en/tours/france-alsace-strasbourg-colmar-paris/

- Type: By plane
- Countries: France
- Duration: 8 days / 7 nights
- Price: 4,200 GEL per person
- Departure: From Kutaisi airport
- Dates: 19–26 Nov 2026, 1–8 Dec 2026, 22–29 Dec 2026

Alsace is one of the most beautiful and photogenic regions of France, where every village looks like it came from an old fairy tale. The tour ends with Paris and Versailles.

**Day 1:** Arrival at Beauvais airport; Reims — a city in eastern France, founded in 80 BC; Hotel check-in
**Day 2:** Walk in Reims; Porte de Mars — an ancient Roman triumphal arch, 3rd century AD; Reims Cathedral (Notre-Dame de Reims) — where the kings of France were once crowned; Metz — a city in north-eastern France; Porte des Allemands; Opéra-Théâtre de Metz — the oldest opera house in France and one of the oldest in Europe; Drive to Saint-Hippolyte, hotel check-in
**Day 3:** Strasbourg (free); Barrage Vauban, 17th century (free); 3 hours of free time to explore the city; Scherwiller; Riquewihr; Return to the hotel
**Day 4:** Eguisheim — named among the most beautiful villages of France in 2003; in 2006 it won a gold medal in the European contest 'Entente Florale'; Ribeauvillé; Kaysersberg; Return to the hotel
**Day 5:** Colmar — the third-largest town in Alsace; Little Venice — a Colmar quarter of canals and half-timbered houses built by the water (optional boat ride); Drive to Paris, hotel check-in
**Day 6:** Eiffel Tower; Pont Alexandre III; Musée d'Orsay; Arc de Triomphe; Champs-Élysées
**Day 7:** Louvre; Notre-Dame de Paris; Sacré-Cœur; Montmartre
**Day 8:** Versailles; Flight from Beauvais airport

Included:
- Flights Kutaisi–Beauvais–Kutaisi
- Hand luggage 10 kg (40x30x20 cm)
- Transfers and travel between cities
- Hotels with breakfast
- Tour escort
- Photography
- Travel insurance

Not included:
- Museum entry fees, optional (130–150 EUR in total)
- Meals other than breakfast
- Transfer to Kutaisi and back (60 GEL)

## 5 Countries in One Tour by Car: France, Switzerland, Germany, Austria, Liechtenstein

URL: https://besttraveler.ge/en/tours/five-countries-alps-switzerland-france-germany/

- Type: By plane
- Countries: Switzerland, France, Germany, Austria, Liechtenstein
- Duration: 8 days / 7 nights
- Price: 4,500 GEL per person
- Dates: on request

A group tour by car through France, Switzerland, Liechtenstein, Austria and Germany. The tour starts and ends in Lyon.

**Day 1:** Arrival in Lyon; Hotel (France)
**Day 2:** Annecy (France) — a town often called 'the Venice of the Alps'; Yvoire — a medieval village on the French shore of Lake Geneva; Château de Chillon; Hotel (Switzerland)
**Day 3:** Gruyères — a medieval Swiss town known for its Gruyère cheese, castle and Alpine views; Château de Gruyères (15 EUR); Jaun Waterfall (Wasserfall von Jaun); Lauterbrunnen — one of Switzerland's most beautiful valleys, the 'valley of 72 waterfalls'; Gimmelwald — an Alpine village above the Lauterbrunnen valley, at about 1,367 m (by cable car); Mürren — an Alpine village above the valley, at about 1,638 m (Gimmelwald–Mürren cable car 35 EUR); Grindelwald — one of Switzerland's best-known Alpine resorts; Hotel (Switzerland)
**Day 4:** Lucerne (Switzerland) — known for its covered wooden bridge built in 1333, with 17th-century paintings inside; Einsiedeln Abbey — a Benedictine abbey dating back to the 10th century; Balzers — a small town in Liechtenstein; Vaduz — the capital of the Principality of Liechtenstein; Lech am Arlberg — a well-known Alpine resort in Austria; Hotel (Austria)
**Day 5:** Linderhof Palace (Germany) — the only one of King Ludwig II of Bavaria's three palaces that he saw completed; Ettal Abbey (Kloster Ettal) — a Benedictine monastery in the Bavarian Alps; Oberammergau — a Bavarian village known for its painted houses, woodcarving and the Passion Play; Hotel (Germany)
**Day 6:** Neuschwanstein (Germany) — one of the most famous castles in the world, built for Ludwig II from 1869; Meersburg — a historic town on Lake Constance (Bodensee); Rhine Falls (Rheinfall), Switzerland; Baden (Switzerland) — a small historic spa town; Basel — a city in north-western Switzerland; Thun (Switzerland) — a town on Lake Thun and the Aare river, known for its medieval castle and old town; Hotel (Switzerland)
**Day 7:** Bern — the Old Town is a UNESCO World Heritage Site; Geneva; Pérouges (France) — a well-preserved medieval village with stone houses, 14th–15th centuries; Hotel (France)
**Day 8:** Lyon — France's third-largest city, known as the capital of gastronomy; its historic centre is on the UNESCO list; Transfer to the airport

Included:
- Return flights
- Hand luggage 10 kg (40x30x20 cm)
- Transport for the whole tour, airport to airport
- Hotels with breakfast
- Tour escort
- Photography
- Travel insurance

Optional extras:
- Cable car Gimmelwald–Mürren–Schilthorn (Piz Gloria, 2,970 m, revolving restaurant where a James Bond film was shot) — 125 EUR (optional)

## Nile Cruise: Luxor, Aswan, Abu Simbel, Hurghada and El Gouna

URL: https://besttraveler.ge/en/tours/egypt-nile-cruise-luxor-aswan-hurghada/

- Type: By plane
- Countries: Egypt
- Duration: 8 days
- Price: 4,500 GEL per person (deposit 1,500 GEL)
- Departure: From Tbilisi airport
- Dates: on request

An 8-day tour of Egypt with a Georgian-speaking tour leader from Tbilisi. It includes St Anthony's Monastery, 4 nights on a 5-star Nile cruise ship, the temples of Luxor and Aswan, and El Gouna.

**Day 1:** Flight from Tbilisi airport at 04:25; Arrival in Hurghada at 09:30; St Anthony's Monastery — the world's oldest working Christian monastery. St Anthony the Great (251–356) lived as a hermit and died in a cave in the cliff above it; Church of St Anthony with very old frescoes; Church of St Paul of Thebes; Old library and manuscripts; Monks' cells
**Day 2:** Luxor; Karnak Temple — one of the grandest monuments of ancient Egypt (20th century BC – 1st century AD); Temple of Hatshepsut — a unique monument of ancient Egyptian architecture (15th century BC); Valley of the Kings — one of the most important necropolises of ancient Egypt (16th–11th centuries BC)
**Day 3:** Hot-air balloon flight (optional, extra cost); Luxor Temple — one of the most elegant and historically important temples of ancient Egypt (14th century BC); Free time on the ship
**Day 4:** Temple of Edfu — one of the best-preserved temples of ancient Egypt, dedicated to the god Horus (237–57 BC); Temple of Kom Ombo — unique because it is dedicated to two gods at once (2nd–1st centuries BC)
**Day 5:** Abu Simbel (optional, 200 USD) — two temples cut into the rock by Ramesses II in the 13th century BC: the Great Temple (Ramesses II) and the Small Temple (Nefertari); Philae Temple — one of the best-known temples in Egypt, dedicated to the goddess Isis; Nubian village (optional, 50 USD) — a small traditional village on the Nile, known for its colourful houses, art and hospitality
**Day 6:** Optional (250 USD): Wadi es-Sebua — an ancient Egyptian temple complex, mostly from the New Kingdom (13th century BC); Optional: Temple of Derr — a small but historically important temple built under Ramesses II (13th century BC); Travel to Hurghada
**Day 7:** El Gouna — a modern resort on the Red Sea coast
**Day 8:** Flight to Tbilisi at 03:20; Arrival at 15:50

Included:
- Round-trip flight Tbilisi–Istanbul–Hurghada
- 20 kg baggage
- Hotels with meals
- 5-star cruise ship (4 nights) with meals
- Transfers
- Travel insurance
- Local guide
- Georgian-speaking tour leader from Tbilisi
- Group excursions
- Entrance fees to historic sites (except optional excursions)

Not included:
- Visa fee (25 USD)
- Optional excursions

Optional extras:
- Abu Simbel — 200 USD (optional)
- Wadi es-Sebua and the Temple of Derr — 250 USD (optional)
- Nubian village — 50 USD (optional)
- Hot-air balloon flight — 90 USD (optional)

## Sicily and Southern Italy — 8-Day Tour from Yerevan

URL: https://besttraveler.ge/en/tours/italy-sicily-palermo-catania/

- Type: By plane
- Countries: Italy
- Duration: 8 days
- Price: 5,700 GEL per person (deposit 1,700 GEL)
- Departure: From Yerevan airport
- Dates: on request

The tour starts with a flight from Yerevan to Italy, follows the coast of southern Italy and crosses to Sicily by ferry. On the island we visit Palermo, Monreale, Agrigento, the baroque towns and Catania.

**Day 1:** Flight from Yerevan at 12:05; Arrival in Naples at 14:15; Salerno, one of the most beautiful towns in southern Italy
**Day 2:** Paola; Sanctuary of St Francis of Paola, an important pilgrimage site in southern Italy where St Francis of Paola rests; Chiesetta di Piedigrotta, a church carved entirely into a seaside rock, with dozens of statues also carved from the rock; Villa San Giovanni; Ferry crossing to Sicily; Messina, Sicily's third-largest city and the main port gateway from mainland Italy
**Day 3:** Cefalù, one of the most beautiful seaside towns in Sicily; Palermo, the capital and largest city of Sicily
**Day 4:** Monreale, a historic hillside town known for its Norman cathedral, built in 1174–1189 by order of King William II; a UNESCO World Heritage site; Marinella di Selinunte; Selinunte Archaeological Park, the largest archaeological park in Europe; Agrigento, founded by the Greeks in the 6th century BC
**Day 5:** Villa Romana del Casale, one of the best-preserved Roman villas; Caltagirone, a historic town in central Sicily known for its ceramics; Ragusa, one of the most beautiful baroque towns in Sicily; Modica, a UNESCO site (Late Baroque towns of the Val di Noto), known as the capital of chocolate
**Day 6:** Marzamemi, a historic fishing village; Noto; Aci Castello castle; Aci Trezza; Catania, Sicily's second-largest city
**Day 7:** Catania; Transfer to the airport; Flight to Tbilisi at 17:40
**Day 8:** Arrival in Tbilisi at 01:35

Included:
- Flight from Yerevan to Italy
- Flights Catania–Istanbul–Tbilisi
- Hand luggage 10 kg (40x30x20 cm) and 20 kg checked baggage
- Minivan transport for the whole tour, airport to airport
- Transfer Tbilisi–Yerevan

# Kazbegi Day Trip from Tbilisi: Route, Drive and What to Wear

URL: https://besttraveler.ge/en/blog/kazbegi-day-trip-from-tbilisi/

Our Kazbegi day tour leaves Tbilisi at 07:00 and is back at about 22:00. You see Dariali Monastery, the big and small Gveleti waterfalls, Gergeti Trinity Church and the Gudauri panorama. The longest walk is to the big waterfall: 1.2 km one way, medium difficulty.

## What you see in one day

Our Kazbegi tour is a straightforward day trip up the Georgian Military Road. We leave Tbilisi in the morning and are back in the evening. The stops are:

- Dariali Monastery complex, in the Dariali gorge, which ends at the Russian border.
- The big Gveleti waterfall: a walk of 1.2 km one way, medium difficulty.
- The small Gveleti waterfall: an easy walk of about 500 m.
- Gergeti Trinity Church, below Mount Kazbek at about 2,170 m above sea level.
- The Gudauri panorama, a viewpoint on the way back.

Ananuri is not on our Kazbegi itinerary. If seeing it matters to you, ask us before you book.

## How long is the drive?

Stepantsminda, the town people call Kazbegi, is about 157 km north of Tbilisi and sits at around 1,740 m. The road crosses the Jvari Pass, its highest point at 2,379 m. Gudauri is about 120 km from Tbilisi at roughly 2,200 m.

The tour leaves at 07:00 and gets back around 22:00, so it is a full day with a lot of time in the vehicle. Get a good night's sleep and bring water and snacks for the road.

## How hard is the walking?

The longest walk on our tour is to the big Gveleti waterfall: 1.2 km one way, medium difficulty, and the same distance back. The path to the small waterfall is easy, about 500 m. If the big waterfall is too much for you, you can visit only the small one.

You will feel the altitude more than you do in the city. If you have heart or breathing problems, ask your doctor before the trip and tell the tour escort.

## What to wear and bring, by season

Mountain weather changes fast and is cooler than Tbilisi. Dress in layers you can take off or put on easily.

- Summer: light clothes plus a warm top, a rain jacket, sunglasses, a hat and sunscreen.
- Spring and autumn: a warm jacket, a hat and waterproof shoes. Paths can be wet or muddy.
- Winter: a winter coat, gloves, a hat and shoes with non-slip soles. Gudauri is a ski resort whose season runs from December to April, so expect snow.
- Any season: comfortable walking or sports shoes, water, snacks and a power bank.
- For Gergeti Trinity Church: women need a headscarf and a skirt, men long trousers.

## Kazbegi or Truso?

The Kazbegi tour is about views and short walks. The Truso Gorge tour has much more walking: 6-7 km one way on an easy path, past colourful travertines, the 'bottomless' lake, Ketrisi village, Abano Convent and Zakagori Fortress. If you enjoy walking, choose Truso. If you want to see a lot without much effort, choose Kazbegi.

## What to do next

The tour page has the price and the latest details. Book a seat early, especially for weekends.

**What time does the Kazbegi tour leave and return?** It leaves at 07:00 and is back at about 22:00.

**Does the Kazbegi tour include Ananuri?** No. Our Kazbegi tour stops at Dariali, the Gveleti waterfalls, Gergeti Trinity Church and the Gudauri panorama.

**How much walking is there?** The longest walk is to the big Gveleti waterfall: 1.2 km one way, medium difficulty. The small waterfall is an easy walk of about 500 m.

**How far is Kazbegi from Tbilisi?** Stepantsminda is about 157 km north of Tbilisi.

**What should I wear?** Dress in layers and bring a rain jacket and comfortable shoes. In winter, wear shoes with non-slip soles.

Sources:
- Wikipedia: Stepantsminda (distance from Tbilisi, elevation): https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stepantsminda
- Wikipedia: Gergeti Trinity Church (elevation): https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gergeti_Trinity_Church
- Wikipedia: Georgian Military Road (Jvari Pass, Darial Gorge): https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Georgian_Military_Road
- Wikipedia: Gudauri (elevation, ski season): https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gudauri

# Best Day Trips from Tbilisi: Where to Go and Who Each Suits

URL: https://besttraveler.ge/en/blog/best-day-trips-from-tbilisi/

For little walking, pick Kakheti, the colourful desert or Kazbegi. If you like hiking, pick Truso (6-7 km one way, easy) or Lagodekhi (8.3 km one way, medium). Go to the mountain routes in the warm months. Kakheti and the lowland routes work for most of the year.

## How to choose

Our day tours leave Tbilisi in the morning (06:00-08:00) and come back in the evening, by minibus with a tour escort. Two things matter most when choosing: how much walking you want and what time of year it is.

## Light walking: history and views

- Kakheti, Sighnaghi and Bodbe: Ninotsminda, Manavi Fortress, Bodbe Convent of St Nino and Sighnaghi. Good for families and older travellers.
- Classic Kakheti: Ujarma, Gombori Pass, Shuamta, Ikalto, Tetri Giorgi and Alaverdi.
- Other Kakheti routes: Nekresi, Ilia Lake, Gremi and Telavi, or Chailuri, Gurjaani Kvelatsminda, Zegaani and Sanagire.
- Kojori and Manglisi: close to the city, with fortresses and churches, ending at the Didgori battle memorial.
- Tianeti: Mamkoda, a bear shelter, Ertso fortress and Sioni Lake.
- Kvemo Kartli: Tserakvi, Gagi Fortress and the Tamarisi lakes.

The Kakheti, Kojori-Manglisi and Dzama tours run in any weather. They are postponed only if there is a problem with the road.

## Desert and easy walks

The colourful desert and David Gareja tour covers Dodo's Rka, the David Gareja monastery complex, the Mravaltskaro colourful mountains and reservoir. Walking is easy, about 1 km in total. If you only want to see the cave monasteries, there is also a Sabereebi tour.

There is little shade in the desert. On warm days bring water, a hat and sunscreen.

## Mountains and waterfalls

- Kazbegi: Dariali, the Gveleti waterfalls, Gergeti Trinity Church and the Gudauri panorama. 1.2 km one way to the big waterfall (medium) and 500 m to the small one (easy). Stepantsminda is about 157 km from Tbilisi.
- Khada Gorge: the confluence of the White and Black Aragvi and the Tskere and Rostiani waterfalls. A 4.2 km walk one way, easy.
- Truso Gorge: colourful travertines, the 'bottomless' lake, Abano Convent and Zakagori Fortress. 6-7 km one way, easy but long.
- Lagodekhi: up the Ninoskhevi gorge to the Gurgeniani waterfall. 8.3 km one way, medium and hard in places. This is the longest trail among our day tours.

## Lakes and the high plateau

- Javakheti lakes: Paravani (Georgia's largest lake), the Poka monastery and convent, Saghamo Lake, Gorelovka and the Madatapa reserve.
- Tabatskuri: over the Tskhratskaro Pass (2,462 m) to Tabatskuri village (2,000 m), with free time at the lake and Timotesubani Monastery. This one leaves at 06:00.
- Samtskhe-Javakheti: Zarzma, Chule, Akhaltsikhe's Rabati and Sapara, with guide Giorgi Beridze-Berjavakhi.

## Which season?

On the high mountain routes (Kazbegi, Truso, Tabatskuri, Javakheti), weather and road conditions decide a lot. Winter there means snow and frost, so plan these for the warm months. Gudauri's ski season, for example, runs from December to April. Kakheti, Gareja, Kojori and Kvemo Kartli are easy to visit at different times of year. The desert gets hot in summer, so spring and autumn are more comfortable there.

Exact dates and prices are on each tour page. If you have a health condition, ask us how much walking a tour involves before you book.

## What to do next

Pick one or two routes, check the tour page and book a seat. If you can't decide, write to us and tell us how much you can walk and who you are travelling with.

**Which day trip is the easiest?** The Kakheti routes, Kojori-Manglisi and the colourful desert, where walking is about 1 km in total and easy.

**Which one is for hikers?** Truso (6-7 km one way, easy) and Lagodekhi (8.3 km one way, medium and hard in places).

**What time do the tours leave?** Most leave at 07:00 or 08:00. Tabatskuri leaves at 06:00. The exact time is on each tour page.

**Can I go to Kazbegi or Truso in winter?** The mountains get snow in winter and road conditions change. Plan mountain routes for the warm months and check winter dates with us.

**Where should I go with children?** The easiest options are the Kakheti routes, Kojori-Manglisi, Tianeti and the colourful desert.

Sources:
- Wikipedia: Stepantsminda (distance from Tbilisi): https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stepantsminda
- Wikipedia: Gudauri (ski season): https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gudauri

# Cappadocia: Best Time to Visit and Hot-Air Balloon Flights

URL: https://besttraveler.ge/en/blog/cappadocia-best-time-hot-air-balloons/

According to GoTürkiye, Türkiye's official tourism portal, the best time for a balloon ride is spring or autumn, when the weather is milder and more settled. Flights start just before sunrise, depend on the weather and can be cancelled. On our tour the flight is optional and costs 200-250 EUR.

## When to go to Cappadocia

GoTürkiye says balloon rides run all year, but the best time is spring or autumn, when the weather is generally milder and more regular than at other times. Its autumn feature names September and October as the best months to enjoy the landscape, when average temperatures drop to milder levels.

Cappadocia lies southeast of Ankara and is best known for its geology, above all the fairy chimneys. The Göreme Open-Air Museum has been on the UNESCO World Heritage List since 1985.

## How a balloon flight works

According to GoTürkiye, flights start just before sunrise. Guests start getting ready around 4:00 am, and a bus collects them from the hotel shortly after.

Everything depends on the weather. Türkiye's Directorate General of Civil Aviation (SHGM) has a separate circular on meteorological evaluation for balloon flights in Cappadocia. In practice, if it is windy or the weather is bad, flights can be delayed or cancelled that same morning.

A balloon flight is never guaranteed. If it doesn't happen, our programme also has time for photos with the balloons in the background. Ask about cancellation and refund terms when you book.

## What a flight costs on our tour

On our 6-day bus tour to Cappadocia, Amasya and Ordu, the balloon flight is optional at 200-250 EUR and is not included in the tour price. On the morning of day 3 you either fly or take photos of the balloons from the ground. The day continues with the Göreme Open-Air Museum, Tokali Church, Uchisar Castle and Pigeon Valley.

## What to wear

- Flights take off at dawn, and mornings are cool, especially in spring and autumn. Wear layers and bring a warm jacket.
- Comfortable closed shoes. Getting in and out of the basket can be awkward.
- A hat, against the sun and the heat from the burner.
- For walking in the valleys: trainers, water and sunglasses.
- For churches and monasteries: covered shoulders.

## Tips

- Book your flight early, with help from the tour escort.
- If you have a health condition, ask your doctor before flying.
- Don't take a cancellation personally: flights are cancelled for safety. The balloons look beautiful from the ground too.

## What to do next

Check dates and price on the tour page. When you book, tell us if you want a balloon flight so we can plan ahead.

**When is the best time for a balloon ride in Cappadocia?** GoTürkiye says spring or autumn. For autumn it singles out September and October.

**Can the flight be cancelled?** Yes. Flights depend on the weather and can be cancelled that same morning if it is windy or the weather is bad.

**How much is the balloon flight on your tour?** It is optional and costs 200-250 EUR. It is not included in the tour price.

**What time does the flight start?** Just before sunrise. Preparation starts at about 4:00 am.

**What should I wear?** Warm layers, a jacket, closed shoes and a hat.

Sources:
- GoTürkiye (official tourism portal of Türkiye): Hot-air balloon: https://goturkiye.com/culturaljourneys/hot-air-balloon
- GoTürkiye press release: Autumn brings out the best of Cappadocia: https://goturkiye.com/branding/press-releases/autumn-brings-out-the-best-of-cappadocia
- GoTürkiye: Cappadocia: https://goturkiye.com/cappadocia
- SHGM (Turkish Directorate General of Civil Aviation): Cappadocia balloon flights meteorological evaluation circular: https://web.shgm.gov.tr/tr/genel-duyurular/5173-kapadokya-bolgesi-balon-ucuslari-meteorolojik-degerlendirme-genelgesi-yayimlanmistir

# Keukenhof 2027: When the Tulip Park in the Netherlands Is Open

URL: https://besttraveler.ge/en/blog/keukenhof-2027-tulip-season-netherlands/

According to the official site keukenhof.nl, Keukenhof is open from Thursday 18 March to Sunday 9 May 2027, daily from 8:00 to 19:00, with last entry at 18:15. Flowering depends on the weather, so nobody can say in advance exactly which week will be best.

## When is Keukenhof open in 2027?

The official Keukenhof website says the park is open from 18 March to 9 May 2027, every day including Sundays and public holidays, from 8:00 to 19:00. Entry closes at 18:15. The address is Stationsweg 166a, Lisse.

The flower season covers these spring weeks, so your travel dates need to fall inside that window.

## When do the tulips bloom?

Keukenhof says the flowering season follows the rhythm of nature and depends on the weather, which makes it hard to name the best time to visit. Early in the season you see early bloomers such as crocuses, daffodils, hyacinths and early tulips. Later, the later varieties come out, including larger tulips. The website also has a bloom report showing current conditions.

## Tickets

- According to the official FAQ, 2027 starting prices for adults are 21 EUR online and 27 EUR at the box office. Children aged 4-17 start at 11 EUR online, and under-4s go free.
- A ticket is valid only for the time slot you book, with no earlier or later entry.
- The site recommends buying online: it is cheaper and guarantees your preferred date and time.
- Visitors spend about 3 hours in the park on average.

If you are on one of our tours, you don't need to arrange a ticket yourself. Keukenhof is in the programme, and the entry price is shown on the tour page.

## How to plan

- Pick dates between 18 March and 9 May. Early and late in the season you see different flowers.
- According to the official site, the park is quieter before 10:30 and after 16:00. Morning and evening light is better for photos.
- Dress in layers and bring an umbrella or rain jacket, because spring weather changes fast.
- Wear comfortable shoes, since you will walk a lot.

## Our tulip tours

We run two 8-day group tours that include Keukenhof:

- Belgium and the Netherlands: flight from Kutaisi. Brussels, Amsterdam, Giethoorn, Volendam, Zaandam, Keukenhof, The Hague, Ghent and Bruges.
- Netherlands and Germany: flight from Tbilisi to Düsseldorf. Castles, Paleis Het Loo, Giethoorn, Zaanse Schans, Amsterdam, Keukenhof and Utrecht.

Spring dates and prices are on the tour pages. If dates aren't listed yet, write to us and we'll hold a place for you.

**When is Keukenhof open in 2027?** According to the official site, from 18 March to 9 May 2027, daily from 8:00 to 19:00, with last entry at 18:15.

**When is the best time to see tulips?** Keukenhof says flowering depends on the weather. Crocuses, daffodils and early tulips come first, and the larger tulips later.

**How much is a ticket?** The official FAQ gives 2027 starting prices of 21 EUR online and 27 EUR at the box office for adults, and from 11 EUR online for children aged 4-17.

**Where do I buy tickets?** On the official site, keukenhof.nl. The ticket is valid only for your time slot.

**Which of your tours include Keukenhof?** The Belgium-Netherlands tour (from Kutaisi) and the Netherlands-Germany tour (from Tbilisi).

Sources:
- Keukenhof official website: https://keukenhof.nl/en/
- Keukenhof official FAQ: https://keukenhof.nl/en/frequently-asked-questions/

# Group Tour Checklist: Documents and Packing for Travel from Georgia

URL: https://besttraveler.ge/en/blog/group-tour-checklist-documents-packing/

Bring a passport valid for at least 6 months after the trip, travel insurance, cash and a card, an adapter, your medicines and hand luggage that fits low-cost rules (10 kg, 40x30x20 cm on our tours from Kutaisi). Under Georgian law, a child under 16 needs one parent's permission and an adult escort. If the child travels without a parent, bring a notarised consent and confirm the details in advance.

## Documents

- Passport: our booking terms require it to be valid for at least 6 months after the trip ends. Check that you have blank pages too.
- A copy or photo of your passport, on your phone and on paper, kept separately.
- Travel insurance: included in most of our flight tours. Save the policy on your phone.
- Tickets and hotel details: the tour escort handles these, but keep your own copy.
- A visa, if the country requires one: check the entry rules with an official source or the embassy.

## Money and cards

- Two cards from different banks, so you have a backup if one gets blocked.
- Tell your bank you're travelling and check your limits.
- Some cash in local currency for small costs, entry tickets and toilets.
- Don't keep all your money in one place.

## Hand luggage on low-cost flights from Kutaisi

Many of our tours from Kutaisi (for example Athens, Vilnius, Bratislava and Brussels) include 10 kg of hand luggage, 40x30x20 cm. That is a small bag, so plan ahead:

- Weigh and measure your bag at home. Extra weight or size costs a lot at the airport.
- Wear your heaviest shoes and jacket instead of packing them.
- Pack clothes that mix and match, and take small toiletry tubes.
- Pack liquids and cosmetics according to the airport's rules.
- Baggage rules can change, so check the exact terms on your ticket.

## Electronics

- Adapter: check the socket type at your destination. In some countries a Georgian plug won't fit.
- Charger and power bank (power banks go in hand luggage only).
- Mobile data: roaming, a local SIM or an eSIM.

## Medicines and health

- Enough of your regular medicines for the whole trip, in their original packaging.
- A prescription or doctor's note if you take strong or unusual medicines.
- A small first-aid kit: painkillers, something for the stomach, plasters and, if you need it, travel-sickness tablets.
- Keep medicines in your hand luggage, not in checked baggage.

## Children: what documents they need

Under Article 8 of the Law of Georgia on the Procedure for Georgian Citizens Leaving and Entering Georgia, a child under 16 may leave Georgia temporarily with the permission of one legal representative (a parent) and must be accompanied by an adult with full legal capacity. A child aged 16-18 who is not in a registered marriage may leave with the consent of one legal representative. If the parents disagree, a court decides.

- The child's own passport.
- Birth certificate, to show that you are the parent.
- If the child travels without a parent (for example with a grandparent or relative), a written consent from a parent certified by a notary. According to the Georgian Notary Chamber, a parent who is abroad can also have the consent certified online.
- Copies of the passport and the consent, kept separately.

The destination country may have its own rules for minors. Before travelling with a child, confirm the rules with the border police, a notary or the country's embassy (as of October 2026).

## What to do next

Choose a tour and check your passport before booking. If you're travelling with a child, prepare the consent early. You can ask us any questions when you book.

**How long must my passport be valid?** Our booking terms require at least 6 months after the trip ends.

**How much hand luggage is included from Kutaisi?** On our Kutaisi tours, 10 kg of hand luggage, 40x30x20 cm. Check your ticket as well.

**Is insurance included?** Travel insurance is included in most of our flight tours. See the 'included' list on the tour page.

**Does my child need the other parent's consent?** Under Georgian law, a child under 16 needs one legal representative's permission and an adult escort. If the child travels without a parent, bring a notarised consent and confirm the details in advance.

**Which medicines should I take?** Your regular medicines for the whole trip, in their original packaging, in your hand luggage.

Sources:
- Law of Georgia on the Procedure for Georgian Citizens Leaving and Entering Georgia, Article 8 (Matsne, consolidated 13/05/2026): https://www.matsne.gov.ge/ka/document/view/93850
- Georgian Notary Chamber: online notarisation of parental consent: https://www.notary.ge/geo-110-mshoblis-tanxmobis-notariulad-damocmeba-onlainrejimshi-iqneba-shesadzlebeli

# Egypt Visa for Georgian Citizens: e-Visa, Fee and Passport (2026)

URL: https://besttraveler.ge/en/blog/egypt-visa-for-georgian-citizens/

Yes, Georgian citizens need a visa for Egypt. Georgia is on the list of countries whose citizens can get an e-Visa on Egypt's official portal: as of October 2026 a single-entry tourist e-Visa costs 30 USD and a multiple-entry one 65 USD. Your passport must be valid for at least 6 months from the day you arrive.

## Do Georgian citizens need a visa for Egypt?

Yes. The e-Visa portal of Egypt's Ministry of Interior (visa2egypt.gov.eg) says that a foreign citizen who wants to enter Egypt generally must first get an e-Visa. Georgia is on the portal's list of countries whose citizens can be issued one.

That means you do not need to visit an embassy. You fill in the form online, pay by card and receive the visa by email.

## How much does the Egypt visa cost in 2026?

As of October 2026, the official portal lists these tourist e-Visa fees:

- Single-entry tourist visa: 30 USD
- Multiple-entry tourist visa: 65 USD

You pay on the website with a credit or debit card. The portal's terms say the fee is non-refundable, so check every detail before you pay.

Our Egypt tours list a 'visa fee of 25 USD' as not included in the price. The official e-Visa portal currently shows 30 USD. Please confirm the exact amount and the type of visa with our manager when you book.

## How to get the e-Visa, step by step

- Go to the official portal visa2egypt.gov.eg and create a personal account.
- Fill in the application with your passport details. Parents can apply for their children from their own account.
- Pay the fee by card.
- Receive the e-Visa by email and print it. You must show the printout at the border.

The portal's home page says you should create your application at least 7 days before departure. Do not leave it to the last minute.

## Passport validity

Your passport must be valid for at least 6 months from your arrival date. The portal does not accept e-Visa applications with diplomatic, service, official and other special passports at this stage; holders of those passports should contact an Egyptian embassy.

## What the border officer may ask for

According to the portal, on arrival you may be asked for:

- a passport valid for at least 6 months from arrival
- the printed e-Visa
- your travel itinerary
- hotel bookings, or details of the places you will visit

The portal also makes clear that an e-Visa is not the final word on entry: the border authorities decide at the port of arrival.

## Visa on arrival and the 'Sinai only' stamp

Many travellers say you can also buy a visa at an Egyptian airport, and that there is a separate free stamp for Sharm el-Sheikh and the South Sinai resorts. We could not confirm either rule for Georgian citizens on the official Egyptian sources we were able to access.

Our advice: do not count on a visa at the airport. Get the e-Visa on the official portal before you fly, or confirm the rules with the Egyptian embassy. If you are going to Sharm el-Sheikh, ask the embassy about the Sinai stamp.

## Watch out for look-alike websites

Many agent websites look official and charge much more for the same visa. The official portal is visa2egypt.gov.eg. Do not enter your card details on any other site.

## Travel to Egypt with us

We run group tours to Egypt from Tbilisi: for example, a 5-day tour of Cairo and Alexandria, a 7-day stay in Hurghada with trips to Luxor and the Suez Canal, or a Lake Nasser cruise. Each tour page shows what is included. Our manager will help with visa questions when you book.

**Do Georgian citizens need a visa for Egypt?** Yes. Georgian citizens can get an e-Visa on Egypt's official portal, visa2egypt.gov.eg.

**How much is the Egypt visa?** As of October 2026 the official portal lists 30 USD for a single-entry tourist e-Visa and 65 USD for multiple entry. The fee is non-refundable.

**How long must my passport be valid?** At least 6 months from the day you arrive in Egypt.

**How early should I apply?** The portal says to create your application at least 7 days before departure.

**Can I get a visa at the airport?** We could not confirm this for Georgian citizens on official sources. The safe option is to get the e-Visa in advance or check with the embassy.

**Does my child need a visa too?** Yes, every traveller needs their own application. Parents can apply for their children from their own account.

Sources:
- Egypt e-Visa Portal, FAQ: who requires a visa, fees, requirements (Ministry of Interior of Egypt): https://www.visa2egypt.gov.eg/eVisa/FAQ
- Egypt e-Visa Portal, Disclaimer (Ministry of Interior of Egypt): https://www.visa2egypt.gov.eg/eVisa/Disclaimer
- Egypt e-Visa Portal, home page (apply at least 7 days before departure): https://www.visa2egypt.gov.eg/eVisa/Home

# Turkey with a Georgian ID Card: Entry Rules for Georgian Citizens

URL: https://besttraveler.ge/en/blog/turkey-entry-with-id-card-for-georgian-citizens/

Yes. According to Türkiye's Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Georgia is on the list of countries whose citizens can enter Türkiye with their national ID card. Georgian citizens do not need a visa for trips of up to 90 days (as of October 2026). A child needs their own valid document.

## Can Georgian citizens enter Turkey with an ID card?

Yes. Türkiye's Ministry of Foreign Affairs publishes a list of 'countries whose citizens are allowed to enter Türkiye with their national IDs'. Georgia is on that list, together with Germany, France, Ukraine, Azerbaijan and others.

This means a Georgian citizen can cross at Sarpi, Vale or another land border, or fly to Istanbul, with a valid Georgian ID card. You can, of course, also travel on your passport.

Check that your ID card has not expired. Airlines may have their own rules on which documents they accept for boarding, so ask before you buy a ticket.

## How long can you stay in Turkey without a visa?

According to Türkiye's Ministry of Foreign Affairs, holders of Georgian ordinary and official passports are exempt from a visa for trips of up to 90 days. That is enough for a holiday, a family visit or a short trip.

The ministry's page does not explain how the 90 days are counted. If you travel to Turkey often or plan a long stay, check the rules with a Turkish embassy or consulate. If you are going to work, study or live in Turkey, ask the embassy which visa or permit you need.

## Travelling on a passport: how long must it be valid?

Under Turkish law, a foreigner's passport must be valid for at least 60 days beyond the end of the permitted stay. For example, for a 90-day stay the passport must have at least 150 days of validity on the day you enter.

Citizens of countries that may enter Türkiye with a national ID card are exempt from this 60-day rule, and Georgia is one of them. Even so, the ministry advises all travellers to have a document valid for at least 6 months from the date of arrival.

## What applies to children

The Turkish ministry's pages do not set out separate rules for children. The basic principle is simple: a child needs their own valid document, either a passport or an ID card. A child cannot travel on a parent's document.

When travelling with a child, check:

- that the child has their own document and it has not expired
- what consent or papers the child needs to leave Georgia if travelling with one parent, grandparents or a group
- the airline's rules for children travelling alone

Check the rules for a child leaving Georgia (for example with one parent or without parents) with the Public Service Hall or the border police before you travel.

## Quick checklist before you go

- A valid ID card or passport for every traveller, including children.
- A planned stay of under 90 days.
- For a child: their own document and, if needed, parental consent.
- If flying: the airline's document rules.

## Travel to Turkey with us

We run tours to Turkey from Tbilisi: bus tours to Trabzon and Sumela, Tao-Klarjeti, Kars, Ani and Van, Cappadocia, and a 7-day tour of Istanbul. Ask our manager which document a particular tour needs when you book.

**Can I enter Turkey with a Georgian ID card?** Yes. According to Türkiye's Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Georgian citizens may enter Türkiye with their national ID card.

**How many days can I stay in Turkey without a visa?** Georgian citizens do not need a visa for trips of up to 90 days (as of October 2026).

**How long must my passport be valid?** Georgian citizens are exempt from the extra 60-day validity rule, but the ministry advises a document valid for at least 6 months from arrival.

**Can a child travel on a parent's passport?** No. A child needs their own valid passport or ID card.

**What does a child need when travelling with one parent?** That depends on Georgia's exit rules. Check with the Public Service Hall or the border police before you travel.

Sources:
- Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Türkiye: Visa information for foreigners (Georgia entry): https://www.mfa.gov.tr/visa-information-for-foreigners.en.mfa
- Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Türkiye: Countries whose citizens are allowed to enter Türkiye with their national IDs: https://www.mfa.gov.tr/countries-whose-citizens-are-allowed-to-enter-T%C3%BCrkiye-with-their-national-id_s.en.mfa
- Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Türkiye: Passport validity requirements while entering Türkiye: https://www.mfa.gov.tr/passport-validity-requirements-while-entering-turkey-in-accordance-with-law-on-foreigners-and-international-protection.en.mfa

# Entering Armenia from Georgia: ID Card or Passport?

URL: https://besttraveler.ge/en/blog/armenia-entry-from-georgia-id-card-or-passport/

Georgian citizens do not need a visa for Armenia. Under an agreement in force since 2023, you can enter Armenia with a biometric ID card through an international border checkpoint, or with your passport. Armenia's Ministry of Foreign Affairs says visa-free foreigners may stay no more than 180 days in a year, unless an international agreement sets a different term.

## Do Georgian citizens need a visa for Armenia?

No. Armenia's Ministry of Foreign Affairs keeps an official list of countries with which Armenia has a visa-free regime under bilateral or multilateral agreements. Georgia is on it for all types of passports. Tourists and people visiting family do not need a visa.

## Can you enter Armenia with an ID card?

Yes. According to Georgia's Ministry of Foreign Affairs, the agreement on visa-free travel between Georgia and Armenia entered into force on 13 July 2023. The prime ministers of the two countries signed it in Yerevan on 12 January 2023.

Under the agreement, citizens of Georgia and Armenia can travel between the two countries with a biometric ID card, through a border checkpoint for international travel. It replaced the old agreement of 1993.

Use only a valid biometric (chip) ID card. If you are not sure your card qualifies, take your passport.

## Which document to take

- Biometric ID card: handy for crossing the land border by bus or car.
- Passport: also accepted. You will need it if you fly on from Armenia to another country, for example from Yerevan airport.

The last point matters: some of our tours to Europe fly from Yerevan airport. On those trips the rules of your destination apply, and for Europe that means a biometric passport.

## How long can you stay in Armenia?

The visa page of Armenia's Ministry of Foreign Affairs says that foreign citizens with a visa-free regime may stay in Armenia for no more than 180 days during one year, unless Armenia's international agreements set a different term.

That is more than enough for a holiday. If you plan a long stay, or want to work or study in Armenia, check the rules with the Armenian embassy.

## Travelling to Armenia with children

According to Armenia's Ministry of Foreign Affairs, foreign minors may enter Armenia with their parents, one parent or another legal representative, or when travelling to join them or a receiving organisation.

A child needs their own valid document. If the child travels without parents or with only one parent, check Georgia's exit rules with the Public Service Hall in advance.

## Quick checklist

- A valid biometric ID card or passport for every traveller.
- Cross at a border checkpoint for international travel.
- Flying on from Yerevan: take your passport and check the destination's rules.
- For a child: their own document and, if needed, parental consent.

## Travel to Armenia with us

We run day trips and multi-day tours to Armenia from Tbilisi: Dilijan, Lori with Haghpat and Sanahin, Jermuk, Tatev and Noravank, and Yerevan with Garni, Geghard and Etchmiadzin. For several of our Armenia tours the tour page says an ID card is enough. We will confirm when you book.

**Do Georgian citizens need a visa for Armenia?** No. According to Armenia's Ministry of Foreign Affairs, the visa-free regime with Georgia covers all types of passports.

**Can I enter Armenia with a Georgian ID card?** Yes, with a biometric ID card, through a border checkpoint for international travel. The agreement has been in force since July 2023.

**How long can a Georgian citizen stay in Armenia?** Under the general rule of Armenia's MFA, no more than 180 days in a year unless an agreement sets a different term. Check with the embassy before a long stay.

**Is an ID card enough to fly from Yerevan to Europe?** No. To fly to Europe you need a biometric passport.

**Does a child need their own document?** Yes. A child needs their own valid passport or biometric ID card.

Sources:
- Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Georgia: Agreement between Georgia and the Republic of Armenia on visa-free travel entered into force (13 July 2023): https://mfa.gov.ge/en/news/305124-aqartvelosa-da-somkhetis-respublikas-shoris-oqalaqeta-ormkhrivi-uvizo-mimosvlis-shesakheb-shetankhme
- Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Armenia: Countries with which Armenia has a visa-free regime under bilateral and multilateral agreements: https://www.mfa.am/en/whoneedvisa
- Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Armenia: Visa (length of visa-free stay, entry of minors): https://www.mfa.am/en/visa/

# Schengen Without a Visa for Georgians: 90/180, Documents, ETIAS

URL: https://besttraveler.ge/en/blog/schengen-visa-free-travel-for-georgian-citizens/

Georgian citizens with an ordinary biometric passport do not need a visa for short stays in the Schengen area: up to 90 days in any 180-day period. Since March 2026 the visa exemption has been suspended only for diplomatic, service and official passports. As of October 2026 ETIAS is not yet in operation and no start date has been announced.

## Is visa-free travel still in place in 2026?

Yes, for holders of ordinary passports. Georgia is listed in Annex II of EU Regulation 2018/1806, among countries whose citizens do not need a visa to cross the EU's external borders for stays of no more than 90 days in any 180-day period.

On 6 March 2026 the European Commission suspended the visa exemption for 12 months, but only for holders of Georgian diplomatic, service and official passports. Ordinary passports are not affected.

The same regulation says that if the problems continue, the Commission can extend the suspension and expand it to all citizens. Check the latest news before you buy tickets.

## The 90/180 rule made simple

You may stay in the Schengen area for up to 90 days in any 180-day period. On every day you are in the area, look back over the previous 180 days: the days you spent in the area during that time must not add up to more than 90.

- The day you enter counts as the first day, the day you leave as the last.
- Days add up across all Schengen countries: Italy, France, Spain and the others count as one area.
- Example: if you spent 30 days in Italy in June and 20 days in Greece in August, those 50 days still count on a trip in October, as long as they fall within the 180-day period.

Ireland does not apply these Schengen rules and has its own entry rules.

## Passport requirements

Under the Schengen Borders Code, your passport must:

- be valid for at least 3 months after the date you plan to leave the Schengen area
- have been issued within the previous 10 years

Georgian law also requires a biometric passport issued within the last 10 years and valid for at least 3 months after the day you leave the EU.

## What border guards in Europe may ask for

Under the Schengen Borders Code, travellers must justify the purpose and conditions of their stay and have enough money for the stay and for the return trip. For tourism or private travel you may be asked for:

- a hotel booking, or an invitation from your host if you stay with someone
- confirmation of an organised trip, or another document showing your travel plans
- a return or round-trip ticket
- proof of sufficient means (each country sets its own reference amounts)

The final decision on entry is made by the border guard. Not needing a visa does not mean automatic entry.

## Checks already at the Georgian border

Since 1 January 2021, under Georgian law, a citizen travelling to an EU or Schengen country may be refused exit at the Georgian border if they cannot show:

- a biometric passport issued within the last 10 years and valid for at least 3 months after the day they leave the EU
- a ticket for leaving the EU or Schengen area, or proof of a booking
- a booking for a hotel or other accommodation, or a host's consent and address
- health insurance valid in the EU
- the means to pay for the trip, or a document proving them

Exit may also be refused to someone who is banned from entering any Schengen country.

Carry all documents with you, printed or on your phone, so you can show them quickly.

## ETIAS: where things stand in October 2026

ETIAS is a new travel authorisation for visa-exempt travellers going to 30 European countries. As of 16 October 2026, the official ETIAS website (travel-europe.europa.eu) says that ETIAS is currently not in operation and that no applications are being collected. The EU will announce the exact start date several months before the launch.

The same site shows an application fee of EUR 20 and stays of up to 90 days with ETIAS. Right now you cannot apply for ETIAS and you do not need it.

Be careful: some websites already offer to 'arrange your ETIAS' for a fee. Official information is only on travel-europe.europa.eu.

## Travel to Europe with us

We run group tours to Europe from Kutaisi and Tbilisi: Rome, Paris, Barcelona and Andalusia, Greece, Belgium and the Netherlands, and the Venice Carnival. Your tour booking, hotel booking and return ticket are exactly the papers asked for at the border, so ask our manager for these confirmations before you travel.

**Do Georgians need a Schengen visa in 2026?** Not with an ordinary biometric passport, for stays of up to 90 days in any 180-day period. Since March 2026 holders of diplomatic, service and official passports need a visa.

**How is the 90/180 rule counted?** On each day, look back over the previous 180 days: days spent in Schengen must not total more than 90. The days you enter and leave both count.

**Which documents should I carry?** A biometric passport, a return ticket, a hotel booking or host's invitation, health insurance and proof of sufficient money.

**Do I need ETIAS now?** No. As of October 2026 ETIAS is not in operation and no applications are collected. The EU will announce the start date several months in advance.

**How much will ETIAS cost?** The official site shows EUR 20.

**How long must my passport be valid?** At least 3 months after your planned departure from Schengen, and it must have been issued within the last 10 years.

Sources:
- Official ETIAS website of the European Union (travel-europe.europa.eu): https://travel-europe.europa.eu/en/etias
- Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2026/496 of 6 March 2026 on the temporary suspension of the visa exemption for nationals of Georgia holding diplomatic, service and official passports (EUR-Lex): https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg_impl/2026/496/oj
- Regulation (EU) 2016/399, Schengen Borders Code: Article 6 entry conditions and Annex I supporting documents (EUR-Lex): https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2016/399/oj
- Law of Georgia No 7069-Iს of 2 September 2020 amending the Law on the Procedure for Georgian Citizens Exiting and Entering Georgia (Article 10, in force from 1 January 2021), Matsne: https://www.matsne.gov.ge/ka/document/view/4978736
